facts.fact_text: In April 2003 a group of farmers held a demonstration in front of the Seimas (the Lithuanian Parliament) building.
The April 2003 demonstration was held to protest about the situation in the agricultural sector with regard to a fall in wholesale prices for various agricultural products.
The April 2003 demonstration was held to protest about the lack of subsidies for producing agricultural products.
The farmers demonstrating in April 2003 demanded that the State take action regarding the situation in the agricultural sector.

At the 16 May 2003 meeting of the Chamber of Agriculture, it was decided to organise protests in three different locations next to trunk roads in Lithuania to draw attention to problems in the agricultural sector.
The demonstrations started on 19 May 2003.
The farmers gathered in the designated areas on 19 May 2003.
Pre-trial investigations against the applicants and a number of other persons were started on suspicion of having caused a riot.
On 4 December 2003 an indictment was brought before the courts.
On 29 September 2004 the Kaunas City District Court found the applicants guilty of having incited riots or having participated in them, under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
The five applicants were each given a sixty-day custodial sentence (baudžiamasis areštas) by the Kaunas City District Court.

The Kaunas City District Court suspended the sentences of all five applicants for one year, finding there was reason to believe that the aim of the punishment could be achieved without actually depriving them of their liberty.

The applicants were ordered not to leave their places of residence for more than seven days without the authorities' prior agreement, for a period of one year whilst execution of the sentence was suspended.
Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code establishes criminal liability for rioting, which is categorised as a public order offence.

Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code provides that a person who has organised or provoked a gathering of persons to commit public acts of violence, damage property or seriously breach public order in other ways, or a person who, during a riot, has committed acts of violence, damaged property or seriously breached public order in other ways, may be sentenced to a custodial sentence (baudžiamasis areštas) or imprisonment for up to five years.
On 29 September 2004 the Kaunas City District Court found the applicants guilty of having incited riots or having participated in them, under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.

The Supreme Court found that the applicants had been sentenced for their crimes under a law which had been valid at the time at which the crimes had been committed and their sentences had been imposed in accordance with the provisions of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
The Kaunas Regional Court observed that the crime of rioting placed in danger public order, society's safety, human health, dignity and the inviolability of property.

The Kaunas Regional Court observed that the objective aspect of the crime of rioting was organising gathered people for a common goal of breaching public order and carrying out that decision, which in the instant case had been to organise the roadblocks.

The Kaunas Regional Court found that as a direct result of the actions of Mr Bronius Markauskas and Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius, on 21 May 2003 a crowd had gone on to a highway and had blocked it, thereby stopping the traffic and breaching the constitutional rights and liberties of others to move freely and without restriction.
The Kaunas Regional Court found that the actions of Mr Bronius Markauskas and Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had caused damage to goods carriers and had thus seriously breached public order.
In May 2003 the Kalvarija municipality issued a permit to hold a peaceful assembly in Kalvarija town, 'near the marketplace'.
In May 2003 the Pasvalys municipality issued a permit to hold a demonstration 'at the car park at the sixty-third kilometre of the Via Baltica highway and next to that highway'.
In May 2003 the Klaipėda municipality issued a permit covering an 'area in Divupiai village next to, but not closer than twenty-five metres from, the Vilnius-Klaipėda highway'.
The permit issued by the Klaipėda municipality specified that Mr Bronius Markauskas was one of the organisers of the gathering.
Mr Bronius Markauskas was informed that he had to observe the law and to adhere to any orders from the authorities and the police in connection with the permitted gathering.

The police record of 22 May 2003 indicates that during the farmers' demonstration on the Kaunas-Marijampolė-Suvalkai highway the farmers and the lorry drivers had a few arguments, but more serious conflicts were avoided.

On 1 September 2003 the Pasvalys police issued a certificate stating that on 19-23 May 2003 the farmers had held a demonstration at the car park at the sixty-third kilometre of the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway.
According to the Pasvalys police certificate of 1 September 2003, on 21 May 2003 at around midday the farmers had gone on to the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway and had stopped the traffic.
According to the Pasvalys police certificate of 1 September 2003, the farmers had only allowed through passenger vehicles and vehicles that carried dangerous substances.
According to the Pasvalys police certificate of 1 September 2003, vehicles that carried goods and cars had been allowed to go through once in an hour and ten at a time on each side of the road.
According to the Pasvalys police certificate of 1 September 2003, the police had attempted to let the traffic bypass the blockade through neighbouring villages in order to ameliorate the situation.

According to the Pasvalys police certificate of 1 September 2003, due to the poor condition of neighbouring roads, not all lorries that carried goods had been able to drive on them and they had had to remain on the highway until the farmers had left it.
According to the Pasvalys police certificate of 1 September 2003, some lorries had become stuck in sand and special machinery had been necessary to pull them out.
According to the Pasvalys police certificate of 1 September 2003, the farmers had unblocked the Panevėžys-Pasvalys-Riga highway at 4 p.m. on 23 May 2003.

The Kaunas City District Court dismissed Mr Bronius Markauskas's claim that he and other farmers had acted out of necessity because the roadblock had been their last opportunity to draw the Government's attention to their problems.

The Kaunas City District Court found that the farmers had had another alternative, namely bringing complaints before the administrative courts, which the farmers had themselves mentioned during the meeting of 16 May 2003.

The Kaunas Regional Court found that the fact that after the roads had been blocked the police and the drivers had negotiated with the farmers with the result that some of the drivers had been let through did not diminish the danger of the offence and its unlawfulness.

The Kaunas Regional Court emphasised that the blockade of a major highway (magistralinis kelias) had had dangerous consequences and could not be considered to have been a mere administrative law offence such as a traffic violation.
The Supreme Court shared the appellate court's view that the applicants could not be considered as having acted out of necessity.

The Supreme Court held that the fall in milk purchase prices and other problems with subsidies for agriculture had not constituted a clear or present danger to someone's property, because the property in question had not yet materialised.
The Supreme Court held that the law protects existing property and that the State had not deprived the applicants of their property.
The Supreme Court held that the applicants' dissatisfaction with the Government's agricultural policy had not justified the acts for which the five applicants had been convicted.

The Supreme Court found that the materials in the case file did not allow the conclusion that the applicants' conviction under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code had been in breach of Article 23 of the Lithuanian Constitution or Article 1 of Protocol No. 1 to the European Convention on Human Rights, because the property in question had not yet materialised.

In Eugen Schmidberger, Internationale Transporte und Planzüge v. Republik Österreich, Case C-112/00 [2003], ECR I-05659, the European Court of Justice found that the fact that the Austrian authorities did not ban a demonstration by protesters which resulted in the complete closure of a single major transit route between Austria and Germany for almost thirty hours was not incompatible with Articles 28 and 29 of the Treaty Establishing the European Community, read together with Article 10 of that Treaty.

The European Court of Justice in Schmidberger found that the restriction of trade in goods between Member States was justified by the legitimate interest in the protection of fundamental rights, in that case the protesters' freedom of expression and freedom of assembly, which applied both to the Community and the Member States.

The European Court of Justice in Schmidberger acknowledged that the national authorities enjoyed a wide margin of discretion in balancing restrictions on intra-Community trade against the protection of fundamental rights, but held that it was for the European Court of Justice to determine whether the restrictions placed upon intra-Community trade were proportionate in the light of the legitimate objective pursued.

The European Court of Justice in Schmidberger acknowledged that whilst a demonstration on a public highway usually entailed inconvenience for non-participants, in particular as regards free movement, that inconvenience could in principle be tolerated provided that the objective pursued is the public and lawful demonstration of an opinion.
